findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a step and an acceptance criterion covering a mixed-version WRITER race on a git remote (old-version force/lease/delete CAS concurrent with a new-version commit-chain write), asserting the outcome is a single owner with no lost lock, or state explicitly why coexisting old writers cannot occur during rollout.
evidence: Step 3 handles only the DATA side: 'A legacy blob tip (rebar <= 0.13 on git remotes) cannot be a parent: write over it once through the existing lease path'
Step 4 and the v0.13.1 _decode_blob AC cover only old READERS, not old WRITERS pushing concurrently

ABSENCE: no AC asserts a new-format writer racing an old-version writer (which still does +/delete/lease-CAS) ends with exactly one owner and no lost lock on a git remote; the mixed-version race ACs (acquire on absent/released, renew vs steal) all assume both racers run the new mechanism
Observation notes S3 is where old writes fail, but git remotes keep working on both versions during rollout
findings.finding: The migration's dual-write window does not cover an old-version writer (bare-blob/lease-CAS push or ref-delete) racing a new-version commit-chain writer during a mixed-version rollout on a git remote, where both code paths can coexist.
scenarios: During rollout a 0.13.x reconciler and a new reconciler share a git-remote tracker; the old one force-writes/deletes refs/reconciler/lock under a lease while the new one chains a commit, producing two believed owners or a silently dropped lock
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the rollout ordering (e.g. all checkouts sharing a tracker must upgrade before any new-format write, or old writers are fenced) and add an AC proving an old-version lease-CAS/delete racing a new-format commit write cannot yield two owners.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'one winner from a non-forced fast-forward push' premise with git-remote-s3's documented bundle-per-push / multi-bundle model (docs/s3-backend.md §5, ADR 0093 §84): state explicitly whether git-remote-s3 performs a server-side fast-forward/ref-ancestry check that rejects a competing non-forced push, cite where that behaviour is observed, and if it does not, redesign the winner-selection mechanism.
evidence: Decision: 'each write ... pushed as a plain non-forced fast-forward from a temporary named ref'

docs/s3-backend.md §5: 'When concurrent pushes leave more than one bundle for the tickets ref, the helper refuses further ref operations' and 'serializes pushes with a per-ref S3 lock' with 'DEFAULT_LOCK_TTL_SECONDS = 60'
ADR 0093 §84: 'Bundle-per-push storage means the multi-bundle state is normal under concurrency'
git-remote-s3 is not importable in this environment (resolve_symbol UNRESOLVED) — the push's fast-forward-enforcement behaviour is Unverified from the plan text and the repo
findings.finding: The plan's central new mechanism depends on an unverified external capability: that git-remote-s3 rejects a competing non-forced (fast-forward-only) push so a race yields exactly one winner. The helper's documented model is the opposite — concurrent pushes both succeed and leave multiple divergent bundles, serialized only by a 60s self-healing per-ref S3 lock (docs/s3-backend.md §5; ADR 0093 §84 'the multi-bundle state is normal under concurrency'). If git-remote-s3 does not perform a server-side fast-forward check across concurrent pushers, both racing acquires/renews land as separate bundles (no loser, no CAS mismatch) and the 'one winner' / RefLockHeldError / LeaseLostError ACs cannot hold.
findings.location: Decision ('pushed as a plain non-forced fast-forward from a temporary named ref'); Plan steps 1-2; ACs 'Two clones racing acquire ... yield exactly one winner', 'A renew racing a steal ... losing renew raises LeaseLostError'
scenarios: Two reconciler clones on an S3 store call acquire on an absent ref within the same push window
A renew races a steal where both pushers hold the 60s S3 lock sequentially but neither sees the other's bundle as the tip

evidence: "the remote format changes by decision"
Step 3 handles new-reads-legacy-blob but not old-rebar-writes-over-new-commit-tip on S3
Observation: old blob-plus-lease push fails on S3

It does not state a back-out path for the case where this change is deployed and then an operator must revert to an older rebar against a store that now holds commit tips.
scenarios: An operator rolls back to rebar <=0.13 after this lands and the S3 store already has commit-tip reconciler refs

evidence: 7 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how a failed tmp-ref cleanup is handled (logged/surfaced vs swallowed) and whether orphaned tmp refs are ever reaped, so cleanup failures are observable rather than silent.
evidence: "drop the temp ref in finally"
No error handling or observability specified for a failed tmp-ref drop
findings.finding: Step 1 drops the temporary `refs/reconciler/tmp/<uuid>` ref in a `finally`, but the plan does not say what happens if that cleanup push itself fails (e.g. a transient S3/helper error), nor whether orphaned tmp refs are surfaced or ever reaped.
scenarios: A tmp-ref delete push fails after a successful write; tmp refs accumulate on the remote across many reconciler passes

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite git-remote-s3's own per-reference S3-conditional-write locking and explain whether the observed delete/`+` races are fundamental to S3 or a helper/version (0.4.2) behavior, and why non-forced ff-only push reliably yields one winner on it.
evidence: Retrieved (awslabs/git-remote-s3, DeepWiki 'Branch Management'): 'git-remote-s3 implements per-reference locking to prevent concurrent write conflicts when multiple clients push to the same branch simultaneously ... uses S3 conditional writes to acquire an exclusive lock for that specific reference'
Plan asserts as established fact: 'On real S3: fast-forward-only pushes from a named ref give one winner; `+` drops the compare; delete has no compare'
Plan pins the helper version ('git-remote-s3 0.4.2') but never references the helper's own concurrency model
Non-goals explicitly excludes 'changing the helper', so the helper's behavior is the substrate the whole mechanism rides on
findings.finding: The plan reframes S3 ref-CAS as something to re-engineer with commit chains without engaging the relevant prior art that git-remote-s3 itself implements per-reference locking via S3 conditional writes to serialize concurrent pushes. The plan's load-bearing positive assertion ('fast-forward-only pushes from a named ref give one winner') most likely holds BECAUSE of that helper-side per-ref lock, yet the plan neither names it nor establishes whether the observed delete/`+` races are a fundamental S3 property or a helper/version (0.4.2) artifact.
scenarios: If a newer git-remote-s3 or a config option already serializes delete/force refspecs, the entire marker-commit redesign may be solving a version-specific gap rather than a fundamental one
Reviewer/operator cannot tell whether ff-only 'one winner' is guaranteed by the helper or incidental to timing

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the failure disposition (retryable CAS-mismatch vs fatal) surfaced when the one-shot legacy-blob lease overwrite in step 3 is itself rejected.
evidence: 'A legacy blob tip (rebar <= 0.13 on git remotes) cannot be a parent: write over it once through the existing lease path from the named ref'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion (and ADR note) asserting the post-rollback state when a downgraded (delete-on-release) version encounters a new-format released/cleared marker, with a literal DATA LOSS RISK note if the old path cannot safely interpret it.
evidence: Step 4: 'Release and clear write marker commits instead of deleting' — this is a one-way change from the prior delete-on-release semantics

The ADR amendment notes 'deleting a live holder's ref lets its next renew re-create it' but there is no assertion about what an old-version RELEASE/clear path does when it encounters a new-format marker after a downgrade
ABSENCE: no AC asserts that after a rollback to a delete-on-release version, a ref left holding a 'released'/'cleared' marker is interpreted correctly (DATA LOSS RISK note absent)
findings.finding: The plan does not assert post-rollback persisted state for the new release/clear markers, which replace ref-deletion with a one-way marker-commit write.
scenarios: Operators roll back to 0.13.x after a new-format release has left a 'released: true' marker commit on refs/reconciler/lock; the old release/steal path's handling of that marker is unverified

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the real-helper scratch-bucket race proof (step 9) ahead of the implementation/docs/test work as an explicit SPIKE gate that must confirm git-remote-s3 rejects a competing non-forced push before steps 1-8 are committed.
evidence: Plan orders implementation (1), classification (2), docs (7), and test rewiring (8) before the real-helper scratch-bucket proof (9)
Observation cites 'moto and a real scratch bucket' — moto does not implement git-remote-s3's bundle-per-push / push-lock behaviour
The non-goals exclude 'CI against real S3', so the only real-helper evidence is the one-off step 9 run
findings.finding: A critical, previously-unproven external capability (git-remote-s3 fast-forward rejection under a real race) is not gated behind a SPIKE: Plan steps 1-8 commit the full implementation, docs rewrite, and test rewiring before the scratch-bucket proof in step 9. The moto backend used in the preliminary evidence does not emulate git-remote-s3's bundle/lock semantics, so the premise is effectively unproven until step 9.
findings.location: Plan step 9 ('Scratch-bucket proof with the real helper') vs steps 1-8; Decision ('Prove the lock operations in a scratch bucket ... before landing')
scenarios: Step 9's scratch-bucket race shows competing pushes both land as bundles, invalidating the mechanism after steps 1-8 are already built
findings.suggested_fix: Reorder: run the two-clone acquire-race and renew-vs-steal proof in the frontier scratch bucket against the real git-remote-s3 helper FIRST; only proceed to steps 1-8 if a competing non-forced push is observed to be rejected (not absorbed into a second bundle).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note in ADR 0031/0093 that commit-chain CAS via non-forced fast-forward push is an established pattern (cf. git-remote-dropbox revision CAS; standard git ff-only push), rather than presenting it as bespoke.
evidence: Retrieved (anishathalye/git-remote-dropbox, DeepWiki 'Push and Fetch Operations'): 'To ensure atomic updates to references, git-remote-dropbox uses a compare-and-swap (CAS) operation leveraging Dropbox's revision-based write modes'
Retrieved (git-scm git-push docs): non-fast-forward pushes are rejected by default — the single-winner property the plan relies on is standard git semantics
Plan frames the mechanism only via internal ADRs ('amend ADR 0031', 'ADR 0093') with no external prior-art anchor
findings.finding: The commit-chain CAS design (write = commit whose parent is the observed tip, pushed non-forced fast-forward from a temp ref; release/clear write marker commits instead of deleting) is an established compare-and-swap-over-a-dumb-remote pattern, not a novel rebar invention, but the plan presents it solely as ADR-0031-amended bespoke design with no reference to that prior art. Stating the provenance would justify the choice as the trodden approach and let reviewers check it against known implementations.
scenarios: A reader evaluating option 4 cannot tell it is a well-known pattern vs a one-off invention, so cannot borrow known pitfalls (e.g. unbounded chain growth, which the plan already flags as a non-goal)
